purpose: Execution-day primary-source recheck for DevBox requirements. Research evidence alone never marks an implementation task PASS.

findings: A client initializes each app-server connection with initialize and initialized before other requests.
The current protocol exposes Thread -> Turn -> Item lifecycle operations including thread/start, thread/resume, thread/fork, turn/start and turn/interrupt with typed notifications.
model/list returns the model catalog available to the current Codex build, including advertised reasoning efforts and related catalog metadata.
modelProvider/capabilities/read exposes provider-level capabilities.
Runtime capability discovery is therefore preferred over invented CLI-version-to-model compatibility thresholds.
devboxImpact: Do not infer GPT model support from a hardcoded Codex semver threshold.
Use app-server model/list as the manual-model catalog when the installed Codex runtime is available; selected-model execution remains the final live task compatibility evidence.
Keep typed thread/turn/item semantics and runtime progress grounded in real provider events.

findings: The Codex app is available on Windows as of the March 4, 2026 update.
Projects and separate threads support multiple agents working in parallel.
Built-in worktree support isolates concurrent work on a repository.
Automations can run scheduled work and surface results in a review queue.
devboxImpact: Maintain Windows-first multi-agent, worktree and review-queue parity targets as benchmark requirements, not copied branding.

findings: NIM LLM exposes OpenAI-compatible inference endpoints including chat/completions, completions, responses and models where supported by the running backend/version.
Management endpoints include health/live, health/ready, metadata, version, license, manifest and metrics.
Liveness only proves the container is running; readiness is distinct, and DevBox still requires a minimal inference for provider READY evidence.
devboxImpact: Keep NVIDIA as a provider adapter, not the DevBox public API.
Use /v1/models for live model discovery and perform a minimal inference before provider READY.
Support a configured local/self-hosted NIM base URL without silently assuming hosted NVIDIA.

findings: NVIDIA documents https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 as the default hosted-model base URL.
The hosted model catalog is available at https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/models and requires provider credentials.
A locally hosted NIM can use its own configured endpoint instead of the hosted base URL.
devboxImpact: Hosted NVIDIA model discovery uses /v1/models with NVIDIA_API_KEY; local NIM can use DEVBOX_NVIDIA_NIM_BASE_URL.
Credential material must never be returned to renderer or activity/evidence payloads.

findings: Latest stable release observed during this check: Hermes Agent v0.18.2, tag v2026.7.7.2.
The release page identifies commit 9de9c25 and shows verified signing metadata.
devboxImpact: Resolve latest stable at execution/install time and record exact tag, commit and integrity provenance instead of hardcoding a forever-version.
Do not surface Hermes as the DevBox product brand.

findings: Vercel documents Local, Preview and Production as default environments.
Custom Environments are documented for Pro and Enterprise workflows.
devboxImpact: Do not flatten Local, Preview, Production and Custom Environments into one generic deployment state.

findings: Queues is documented as durable event streaming with consumer groups, retries and at-least-once delivery semantics.
Consumers must be designed for idempotency because redelivery is possible.
Queues is the lower-level message primitive; Workflow is the higher-level durable multi-step orchestration abstraction.
devboxImpact: Model Queue and Workflow separately and require idempotent consumers for at-least-once queue delivery.
